item.title: 3.0b3
item.description:
## New
- Overhauled the app to add playlists, track versions, and culling. - The old version was great for comparing multiple versions of a single track. Now you can use it to compare multiple versions of entire albums. - The playlist also makes it a handy little audio player in its own right. - Major redesign. Collapsed the UI into a compact window with prominent artwork display. - Toggle the artwork, playback controls, and playlist to make the player more compact as needed. - Added a playlist with versions. - Any track in the playlist can have multiple versions. - Takes auto-groups likely versions of the same track by default, and you can group, ungroup, and reorder them yourself. - Added support for culling tracks. - Mark items as rejected, which skips them during playback and comparison. - Still to come are features to build on top of this: adding non-rejected tracks to an iTunes playlist, copying them, deleting rejected tracks.
## What Needs Testing - Should culling consist only of marking tracks as rejected, or do we need the ability to pick as well? What would you do with picked tracks vs. standard tracks that haven't been rejected?
## Changes Since 3.0b2 - Hold Shift while dropping audio files onto Takes to open them together in a new comparison, even when automatic grouping is off. - Automatic grouping matches track titles across live takes, edits, and other versions, even when artist tags or track lengths differ. - Nudging the offset in Compare applies it when you press Return or leave the field, instead of on every nudge. Press Esc to discard the edit. - Rebuilt the app icon in vector form, and gave beta builds a distinct icon. - Lots of little behavior and edge case refinements.
## Changes Since 3.0b1 - Waveforms reappear faster when you reopen a comparison during the same app session. - The Compare button and now-playing speaker are easier to see when the row is highlighted - File drops highlight the artwork and playback controls along with the playlist area. - Use Reset Offset or Reset All Offsets in the Playback menu to clear timing adjustments in Compare. - Press Esc in Compare to clear the selected loop instead of navigate back to the playlist. - Switch Track and Switch & Repeat now skip versions whose files are missing. - Playlist commands no longer act on hidden playlist rows while Compare is open. ⌘R applies to the active version in Compare. - Navigating back to Playlist mode while tempo alignment is in progress cancels the alignment processing. - Artwork stays steady while you show or hide the Player or Playlist.

item.title: 3.0b1
item.description:
## New
- Overhauled the app to add playlists, track versions, and culling. - The old version was great for comparing multiple versions of a single track. Now you can use it to compare multiple versions of entire albums. - The playlist also makes it a handy little audio player in its own right. - Major redesign. Collapsed the UI into a compact window with prominent artwork display. - Toggle the artwork, playback controls, and playlist to make the player more compact as needed. - Added a playlist with versions. - Any track in the playlist can have multiple versions. - Takes auto-groups likely versions of the same track by default, and you can group, ungroup, and reorder them yourself. - The auto-grouping logic needs testing. - Added support for culling tracks. - Mark items as rejected, which skips them during playback and comparison. - Still to come are features to build on top of this: adding non-rejected tracks to an iTunes playlist, copying them, deleting rejected tracks. - Do we need the ability to pick as well as reject? What would you do with picked tracks vs. standard tracks that haven't been rejected?

## New
- Major performance improvements throughout the app - Files open quicker - Waveforms render much faster and the UI remains responsive while loading - CPU usage is drastically reduced - Playback with 1 track has been reduced from 40% → 2.5% (comparable to QuickTime player) - Playback with 20 tracks has been reduced from 103% → 8% (less than QuickTime Player at 32%) - Idle CPU consumption is now 0% - (All measurements taken with an M1 MacBook Pro) - UI responsiveness is vastly improved - Zooming, scrolling, and playhead-following is fluid, even with dozens of files open - Dragging to rearrange tracks animates smoothly - Playhead glides continuously instead of ticking along
## Improved
- Loops are now gapless, wrapping seamlessly to the beginning of the next loop - Quickly adjust a track's offset without selecting the input field using new keyboard shortcuts - Improved waveform interactivity - The playhead can be dragged in the waveform area (previously dragging was limited to the grabber in the ruler area) - Clicking on a waveform switches playback to that track (previously you had to click in the info column) - Quick Open from Finder now supports folder selections - Added haptic feedback to the zoom slider - Inertial scroll during playback behaves naturally: it settles to a stop before jumping to the playhead, rather than fighting with playhead-follow and causing jerkiness - Refined the app's visual design, icons, and hit targets throughout
## Fixed
- Mouse cursor reliably changes state when hovering over overlapping UI elements to show which interaction has priority - Tooltips are only shown when text has been truncated - Shrunk the hit target of the "Click Here to Compare" button to prevent accidental clicks when there are no tracks loaded - Blind Listening Mode is disabled when no tracks are loaded

## Fixed
- Creating a loop no longer moves the playhead if it's already within the loop range

## New - Resizable track info column. Grab the divider and drag it left/right
## Improved - Changing the loop range during playback no longer causes audio to stutter
